subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Qualitative market research data is most useful for understanding:
options: Exactly how many units were sold
Customers' opinions, motives and feelings
The total revenue figure
The business's fixed costs
questions.explain: Qualitative data explores opinions and reasons behind customer behaviour rather than just numbers.

questions.q: Price skimming is most suitable for:
options: Everyday low-cost goods
Loss-making products only
A new, innovative product with little competition
Products at the decline stage
questions.explain: Skimming charges a high initial price for new, innovative products before competitors enter.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an extension strategy?
options: To launch a brand new product
To reduce the number of customers
To stop all advertising
To prolong the life of a product and delay decline
questions.explain: Extension strategies (e.g. new packaging or features) aim to extend the maturity stage and delay decline.

questions.q: Quantitative data is best described as:
options: Always more expensive to collect
Data that cannot be analysed
Numerical data that can be measured
Opinions and feelings about a product
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and measurable, such as how many people prefer a product.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of strong branding for a business?
options: It guarantees no competition
It allows the business to charge higher prices and build customer loyalty
It removes the need for any marketing
It increases variable costs
questions.explain: A strong brand builds customer loyalty and often allows a business to charge a premium price.

questions.q: An increase in competition is likely to:
options: Put pressure on a business to lower prices or improve quality
Have no effect on the business
Always remove the need to advertise
Guarantee higher profits
questions.explain: More competition pressures businesses to compete on price, quality or service to keep customers.

questions.q: If interest rates rise, what is a likely effect on businesses?
options: The cost of borrowing increases, which can reduce investment and consumer spending
Inflation always falls to zero
Exports automatically increase
Borrowing becomes cheaper
questions.explain: Higher interest rates raise borrowing costs and can reduce both business investment and consumer spending.

A general rise in the price level over time
A fall in the number of workers
A rise in interest rates only
questions.explain: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general level of prices in an economy.

questions.q: High unemployment in the economy is likely to mean:
options: Higher demand for luxury goods
Consumers have more money to spend
No effect on businesses
Lower consumer incomes and reduced demand for many products
questions.explain: High unemployment lowers overall incomes and tends to reduce demand for many goods and services.

questions.q: A possible benefit to a business of international trade is:
options: Access to larger markets and more customers abroad
No need to consider exchange rates
Guaranteed protection from competition
Lower quality requirements
questions.explain: International trade gives businesses access to larger markets and new customers overseas.

questions.q: During a recession (a downturn in the business cycle), businesses often experience:
options: Rising consumer spending
Falling demand and lower sales
Guaranteed higher profits
No change at all
questions.explain: In a recession consumer spending falls, so many businesses see lower demand and sales.

questions.q: How can new technology act as an external influence on a business?
options: It never changes how businesses operate
It can create new products and ways of selling but requires investment
It always lowers all costs immediately
It removes the need for any staff
questions.explain: Technology creates new products and selling methods but often needs investment and training to adopt.
